text: You already have a color palette. It's in `prereqs/tokens.json`, exported from Figma file AqpBpdKicUBczcUwdiDEnk on Oct 30, with Light and Dark modes. In short: | Role | Name | Hex | |---|---|---| | Primary | Orchestration Blue | `#0538FF` | | Ink (text, dark background) | neutral/975 | `#0B0B12` | | Paper | neutral/0 | `#FFFFFF` | | Agent activity | Mist (blue/200) | `#B8C4FF` | | Needs-you / warning | Signal | `#FF5A1F` | | Success | success/500 | `#1F9D55` | | Danger | danger/500 | `#D7193A` | Behind that core are full ramps: 14 neutral steps, 10 blue, and 5–6 each for signal, success and danger. About 40 semantic tokens map those ramps to Light and Dark. The usage rules are already in `concept.md`. For example, the blue mark only goes on light backgrounds, text on Signal is always Ink, and Mist is never used for text on white. So this is a choice of direction rather than a fresh build: **How should the kit's color page treat this palette?** - **A. Keep it and lead with the core (recommended).** The Color page opens with the 5 brand colors above (Blue, Ink, Paper, Mist, Signal). Success and danger come next as status colors, and the full ramps and semantic tokens go underneath for designers. Nothing existing changes. - **B. Cut it down.** Reduce the palette to the core colors plus a short neutral ramp. This removes existing tokens, so I'd need your approval for each change. - **C. Start over.** Pick a new palette direction. This replaces your Figma variables, which the kit rules don't allow without your explicit sign-off. Also, `prereqs/brand-spec.md` doesn't exist yet. The Brand Kit Musician needs a signed-off spec before it can build. If you go with A, I can write the color section of that spec from `tokens.json` and `concept.md` so you can sign it off. Briefing Musicians isn't connected in this version of Orchestra yet, so the Figma build can't start until it is. I haven't opened the Figma file. Everything above comes from the exported `tokens.json`, so if the file has changed since Oct 30, these values may be out of date.
